children: Acadia Pharmaceuticals reached a preliminary court-approved settlement of a stockholder derivative action requiring adoption of corporate governance reforms and a $1,500,000 fee for stockholders' counsel.
Court preliminarily approved settlement of Kanner v. Biggar involving derivative claims tied to pimavanserin disclosures.
Company will adopt and maintain specified corporate governance reforms for at least four years to strengthen disclosure and oversight.
Parties agreed a mediator-proposed Fee and Expense Amount of $1,500,000 to be paid to Stockholders’ Counsel, subject to court approval.
Settlement hearing set for January 13, 2027; objections must be filed by December 23, 2026 per notice.
If approved, the Action will be dismissed with prejudice and releasations will extinguish specified derivative claims (excluding securities class and opt-out actions).
